lines.name: Classical (Mar del Plata)
lines.intro: In the King's Indian you let White build a big center, then hit it with ...e5. When White closes the center with d5, you attack on the kingside while White attacks on the queenside.

notes.0: White opens with the queen's pawn.
notes.1: Develop and stop e4 for now.
notes.3: Get ready to fianchetto your bishop.
notes.5: The bishop aims down the long diagonal at White's center.
notes.7: Control e5 and get ready for ...e5.
notes.11: The key move: strike at the center.
notes.14: White closes the center and gains space on the queenside.
notes.15: The knight reroutes toward the kingside. Next come ...Nd7 and ...f5.

lines.name: Sämisch (5.f3)
lines.intro: In the Sämisch, White plays f3 to cement e4 and often castles long to attack. Strike with ...e5, and after d5 bring your knight to h5 to prepare ...f5.

notes.0: White opens with the queen's pawn.
notes.1: Develop and stop e4 for now.
notes.3: Get ready to fianchetto your bishop.
notes.5: The bishop aims down the long diagonal at White's center.
notes.7: Control e5 and get ready for ...e5.
notes.8: The Sämisch: f3 protects e4 and prepares Be3 and Qd2.
notes.13: The knight heads to h5 to support ...f5.

lines.name: Fianchetto (g3)
lines.intro: Against White's fianchetto, play ...d6, ...Nbd7 and ...e5. White's position is solid, so you aim for a sturdy center and long-term pressure.

notes.0: White opens with the queen's pawn.
notes.1: Develop and stop e4 for now.
notes.3: Get ready to fianchetto your bishop.
notes.6: White fianchettoes too, guarding the king.
notes.8: White's bishop takes the long diagonal.
notes.15: Prepare ...Qa5 or ...Qb6 and a later ...d5 or ...b5.
